contexts.text: In each thing in the inmost sense is the marriage of the Lord's Divine Human with His Kingdom and Church; nay, in the supreme sense there is the union of the Divine Itself and the Divine Human in the Lord.
And in the inmost and supreme sense there is the Divine marriage which is in the Lord; thus the Lord Himself.
The Word in its inmost sense treats of the Lord alone.
The Lord Himself, who is the all in all things of the Word in its inmost sense.
Therefore the Word in its inmost and supreme sense treats of the Lord alone; and especially of the glorification of His Human. Hence comes all the Holy of the Word. AC 10370.

In the Word there are the external sense, the internal sense, and the inmost sense... The Word in its inmost sense is celestial, being accommodated to the perception of the Angels in the Lord's Celestial Kingdom. AC 2802.
The doctrine of celestial good... is contained in the inmost sense of the Word. AC 7258.
The celestial Angels... perceive the Word in its inmost sense. References.
In its ultimate sense the Word is natural; in its interior sense it is spiritual; and in its inmost sense it is celestial.
These are in the inmost sense, which treats of the Lord.

He told me what each thing signified; not what the sense of the letter, nor what the interior or spiritual sense, but what the inmost sense which is celestial. This he saw, not from the words, but from the letters and their flections and curvings...
The celestials have [the Word] according to the inmost sense.

In the Inmost sense is the Lord alone; for it treats there about Him, the glorification of His Human, the ordination of the Heavens, the subjugation of the Hells, and the establishment of the Church by Him; and therefore, in the inmost sense, each of the tribes = the Lord as to some attribute and work of His.
The inmost or celestial sense is for the inmost or Third Heaven.
